key_insight: Extending tabulated chemistry with preferential and differential diffusion in RANS lets the model capture lean hydrogen flame thermo-diffusive behavior much more faithfully than unity-Lewis-number assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This improves the predictive reliability of low-cost CFD for hydrogen combustor and burner design, where flame length, heat release, and stability are strongly affected by non-unity transport.
method: RANS tabulated-chemistry model augmented with preferential and differential diffusion.
Progress-variable and mixture-fraction transport equations derived from species equations using mixture-averaged diffusion and Soret effect.
Turbulence-chemistry interaction handled with a presumed PDF closure.
evidence_signal: Validated against DNS for a lean premixed H2-air slot burner at Re=5500 and 11000, reproducing flame length, heat-release distribution, and key equivalence-ratio/super-adiabatic temperature branches.
watch_item: Performance depends on turbulence closures for turbulent diffusion, scalar dissipation rate, and Reynolds stresses, so calibration and closure choice can materially affect results.
paper_title: Preferential and differential diffusion in RANS simulation of lean hydrogen flames with tabulated chemistry
